answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, skip the 22-miler. With the race now on Oct 18, a 22 this close would cost more than it gives: the legs would still be absorbing it on race morning, and the fitness gain from mile 20 to 22 is tiny compared with the recovery cost.

You already have a 20 and a 17 in the bank, both run strong and controlled. One more long run of 16 mi with marathon-pace miles on Sun Oct 4 gives you the specific work you need, then we taper. That is the right call for a sub-3:45.

new.analysis:
## How last week landed
You executed the full week exactly as laid out: 42 mi, five runs, every session done. The 17-miler on Sunday was the standout, with the back half one second per mile faster than the front and heart-rate drift of under 5 bpm. That is a well-paced long run on tired legs, and it tells me the aerobic base is in good shape.

The Wednesday threshold hit the right paces, with three reps around 7:58/mi and no fade. Heart rate climbed about 18 bpm across the session, which is on the higher side but expected for threshold work in week four of a push.

## Why this plan
The race moving two weeks forward means the week of Sep 28 is now your last real training week, not a stepping-stone to a bigger one. The job this week is to touch marathon pace twice (short on Wednesday, longer on Sunday) and then back off.

Marathon pace for sub-3:45 is 8:35/mi. The Wednesday session is a dress rehearsal for that feel, and the Sunday long run of 16 mi with 6 at marathon pace in the middle is the specific workout that most predicts race day. After that we drop volume by about 25 percent the following week and more the week of the race.

## What I am not doing
No new distance peaks, no new workout types, and no doubles. Your friend's 70-mile weeks are not your plan: changing load this close to a race is where injuries and bad races come from. Hold the shape that has worked.
